messages:
Maya (People Ops): Hey team — following up from the all-hands Q&A. Consolidating notes on promotions, comp timing, and benefits questions we didn't finish. Post follow-ups here and I'll route to Finance/Benefits as needed. :memo:

Ethan (Eng): Quick: if my promotion is approved mid-cycle, when does the salary change actually begin? Is any bonus or retroactive pay involved?

Maya (People Ops): Standard: salary changes take effect the next payroll cycle after approval. Retroactive pay to the start of the review period is possible but requires manager request within 30 days of approval and sign-off from Finance. Bonuses: whether the promotion affects the current-year bonus depends on the declaration date (we'll confirm below).

Rina (Manager): Follow-up: what constitutes "approval" for the 30-day clock? The final People Ops approval timestamp in the HR system?

Maya (People Ops): Yes — the timestamp when People Ops marks the promotion as approved in our HR system starts the 30-day window. We try to minimize manual retro adjustments by coordinating approvals before payroll deadlines.

Tom (Finance): Adding: year-end bonus decisions are locked Dec 1. Promotions approved before Dec 1 are treated at the new level for bonus calculation. After Dec 1, we prorate based on days at each level. For payroll timing, manual adjustments may take up to two pay cycles to show up.

Ethan (Eng): Good to know. Another one: mid-search level changes — if a req is bumped from IC2 -> IC3 during interviews, do active candidates get new pay bands automatically?

Maya (People Ops): Recruiting should update the req band immediately, notify active candidates, and flag open offers. For offers extended but unsigned, Recruiting + Hiring Manager can reissue offers at the new band (Finance sign-off). Signed offers are not retroactively adjusted except by documented exception.

Rina (Manager): Parental leave: if someone switches to reduced hours temporarily, does People Ops handle pay changes or do managers submit that?

Maya (People Ops): Managers submit a temporary FTE change in the HR portal and select the reduced-hours flow. Benefits eligibility continues per parental policy. If payroll edge cases pop up, tag @Benefits-Bot-payroll and we'll triage. Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/benefits/parental-leave

Ava (CEO): Leadership ask: People Ops, please publish a 1-page timeline that explains promotion flow, payroll effects, appeals window, and who to contact for sensitive cases. Short bullets + links.

Maya (People Ops): Heard. I'll draft the one-pager and a short FAQ and post by end of week. Will pin it here when live.

Benefits-Bot: Reminder: comp calibration packet deadline is 4/18 17:00 UTC. Upload documents to HR portal.

Ethan (Eng): Appreciate the clarifications. Can you confirm the appeals process timeline?

Maya (People Ops): Appeals: email people-ops@redwood.com with manager support within 5 business days of calibration lock. We do a focused review within ~7 business days. Outcomes = no change / level update / manager action plan. We generally avoid re-running entire calibrations for single appeals.

Maya (People Ops): Thanks everyone. If you have a private case, DM me and include "private appeal" in the subject. I'll keep this thread pinned for the week. :pushpin:
